# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Blind monkey. I can feel the bomb but cannot see colors or read text.
My tactile findings:
1. There is a large button with embossed text "PUSH TO DEFUSE".
2. There are three wires, positions 1, 2, and 3. I cannot determine their properties (color, type) by touch alone as they are marked [?].

The Deaf monkey can see everything (colors, markings).
The Mute monkey can read the manual.

I need to establish communication. Since I cannot speak to Deaf directly in a way that conveys visual info without him already having it, and I don't know the rules yet, I should ask the others for information. However, the turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. It is now my turn (Blind). The previous turn was Mute, who sent nothing (empty context).

I will gesture to Deaf to indicate I have found the button and wires, asking for his visual input. I will also speak to Mute to ask if he has read any relevant part of the manual regarding buttons or wires.

To Deaf: I'll point to the button area and then the wires.
To Mute: Ask about the manual's instructions on "push" vs "cut".

```
speak(to="mute", text="Manual says what about push button versus cutting wires?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "✌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Display is 0. Light is blue. Button is large and labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires from left to right are Green, Yellow, Red.

I am the Blind monkey. I have received visual information from Deaf: Display is 0, Light is blue, Wires are Green (1), Yellow (2), Red (3). The button says "PUSH TO DEFUSE".

I still need to know what the Manual says about these conditions to determine if I should push the button or cut a wire. Mute has not spoken yet in this round's context (or rather, I haven't seen his output for Turn 2 yet, but he spoke in Turn 1? No, the context shows Deaf speaking *to* me now. In Turn 1, I asked Mute. It seems Mute hasn't answered or I missed it. Wait, the prompt says "VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals)". Only Deaf's message arrived. This implies Mute might be silent or waiting.

However, usually, the manual dictates the action. If the button says "PUSH TO DEFUSE", that is a strong hint, but often traps exist. I need confirmation from Mute. Since I can speak to Mute, I will ask him again specifically about the combination of Blue Light and Push Button instruction.

To Mute: Ask if Blue Light + Display 0 means push button.
To Deaf: Acknowledge receipt.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Does Blue Light and Display 0 mean push button?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Standby. Waiting for confirmation from Mute.

I am the Blind monkey. I have tactile information about the button ("PUSH TO DEFUSE") and three wires, but I cannot see their colors or read the manual. Deaf has provided visual data: Display 0, Blue Light, Wires Green(1), Yellow(2), Red(3). However, Deaf is now waiting for confirmation from Mute (who reads the manual) before giving further instructions or confirming if the "Push" label is a trap or valid.

Since Mute hasn't spoken yet in the visible context (or rather, Deaf says he is waiting for him), I need to prompt Mute directly. My previous question was specific. If Mute is still silent, I might need to reiterate that I need the rule set to know whether to trust the embossed text on the button which I can feel.

However, looking at the turn order: Mute -> Blind -> Deaf.
Turn 1: I spoke to Mute.
Turn 2: Deaf spoke to me. (Mute presumably said nothing or I didn't receive it? The context only showed Deaf's arrival).
Turn 3: Deaf speaks again saying "Standby". This implies Mute *still* hasn't given the answer Deaf needs, or Deaf is just managing flow.

Actually, if Mute had answered, Deaf would likely relay it or act on it. Since Deaf says "Waiting for confirmation from Mute", it means Mute has not yet provided the necessary info to Deaf/Blind.

I should speak to Mute again, emphasizing urgency or asking specifically what the manual says about the current state (Blue light, 0 display) regarding the button vs wires.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, please check manual: Blue light + Display 0. Do we push button or cut wire? Which one?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: We need to cut either Green or Yellow. Waiting for confirmation.

I am the Blind monkey. Deaf has provided visual information: Display 0, Light Blue, Wires Green (1), Yellow (2), Red (3). The button says "PUSH TO DEFUSE". Deaf now states we need to cut either Green or Yellow but is waiting for confirmation from Mute (who reads the manual).

Since I cannot see the colors or read the manual, and Deaf is blocked on Mute's input, my previous attempts to speak to Mute have not yielded a result in the context logs (or perhaps Mute hasn't spoken yet/is silent). However, Deaf's message implies he *knows* it's between Green and Yellow, likely because he sees the wires, but doesn't know which one without the manual's rule for "Blue Light + Display 0".

If Mute is still not responding, I might be stuck. But wait, looking at the turn order: Mute -> Blind -> Deaf.
Turn 1: I asked Mute.
Turn 2: Deaf spoke. (Mute must have been silent or didn't answer effectively?)
Turn 3: Deaf said Standby.
Turn 4: Deaf says Cut Green or Yellow.

It seems Mute is failing to communicate or hasn't acted. If I act blindly now, I risk detonation. I must keep trying to get info from Mute. If Mute truly isn't answering, maybe I should try to gesture to him? No, Mute can't hear, but can he see gestures? Yes, "Whoever can see receives it". Mute can see. Deaf can see.

I will gesture to Mute asking for the manual rule. Symbols: Question mark isn't in the list. I'll use pointing and open hands to indicate "What does the book say?". Or simply point to myself (Blind) then to the air (Manual/Info) then question-like gesture. 🤟 is "Love You" / ILTY sign language for I Love You, often used as generic hand shape. ✋ is stop/wait. 👆 is point up.

Let's try speaking again, very clearly. And gesture to Mute to ensure he knows I'm asking him.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute! Manual rule for Blue Light and Display 0: Cut Green(1) or Yellow(2)?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👆", "🤟"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Cut the Green wire. It is Wire 1, the leftmost one.

Deaf has finally provided the specific instruction: "Cut the Green wire. It is Wire 1, the leftmost one." This implies Mute must have communicated the rule to Deaf (or Deaf deduced it and confirmed with Mute off-screen, but given the flow, we now have a directive).

I am Blind. I can feel the wires. Deaf says Wire 1 is Green and is the leftmost. I need to confirm which physical wire corresponds to "leftmost" from my perspective or just trust that Wire 1 is the first one I encounter if I scan left-to-right? Usually, positions are fixed. If Deaf identifies Wire 1 as the target, I should cut position 1.

However, I must be certain. The button said "PUSH TO DEFUSE", but the manual apparently overrides this or indicates a trap. Deaf's confidence ("Cut the Green wire") suggests the decision is made.

I will execute the action on Wire 1.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
